# #740 — policy_safety guard fails closed on multi-line quoted commands and convicts quoted prose, with a misleading branch-unreadable message

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: bug
Created: 2026-08-23T19:44:07Z
Updated: 2026-08-23T19:44:07Z

---

Measured 2026-08-23 on the Mac mini, Claude Code session in
`/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development`, branch `wip/2026-08-23` (not protected,
branch state readable, `git branch --show-current` returns in 7ms).

Three consecutive legitimate commit attempts were refused by the packaged
guard (openbrain-provider,
`site-packages/openbrain_provider/policy_safety.py`) with:

    Codex git guard: unable to verify the current branch; commit/push is
    blocked until branch state is readable.

All three used a quoted multi-line `-m` message (conventional subject +
body). The identical commit from the identical cwd succeeded immediately
when the message moved to a file (`git commit -q -F <msgfile>`), which
rules out the subprocess/cwd path and implicates
`_git_history_block_reason`: when `_history_mutators(command, command_cwd)`
raises ValueError (shell parse failure on the multi-line command) and
`_GIT_MUTATES_HISTORY` matches, the guard fails closed and reuses the
branch-unreadable message.

It then reproduced on a NON-git command: a `gh issue create --body "..."`
whose body text merely DESCRIBED the defect (contained `git commit -m`
spellings inside a quoted multi-line string) was blocked the same way.
That is the #147/#164 shape the TS gate
(`_ob/scripts/policy-refresh-gate.ts`) already documents and fixed by
parsing per-command argv: the Python port matches substrings of the raw
line when its parser bails, so prose about a commit convicts the command
carrying it.

Three defects:

1. The parser rejects a command shape git itself accepts (quoted
   multi-line `-m`), so the guard blocks the exact commit-message style
   GIT_STANDARDS asks for.
2. On parse failure the fallback regex runs over the WHOLE submitted text,
   quoted data included, so non-git commands (gh, printf, cat) are
   convicted by their own string contents.
3. The refusal text names the wrong cause. "Branch state unreadable" sends
   diagnosis toward git/cwd/timeout; the actual failure was command
   parsing. The parse-failure path should say it could not parse the
   command and name the offending construct.

Repro:

    cd /Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development   # any non-protected branch
    git add <some-file>
    git commit -q -m "subject line

    body line one"
    # -> blocked with branch-unreadable message
    git commit -q -F msg.txt              # same content -> passes

    gh issue create --body "text containing: git commit -m \"x
    y\""
    # -> also blocked

Workaround until fixed: move multi-line content to files
(`git commit -F`, `gh issue create --body-file`).
